data.title: 815MNB to Showcase Neuraon Assist Wellness Headband at CES 2027
data.description:
815MNB to Showcase Neuraon Assist Wellness Headband at CES 2027

- Real-time heart rate and HRV monitoring automatically adjusts noninvasive vagus nerve stimulation (VNS)

- Hands-free relaxation and pre-sleep unwinding without complex data charts or manual app controls

- Expanding R&D from consumer wellness into clinical therapeutics targeting a 2028 commercial launch

815MNB, a South Korean wearable health-tech company (CEO Yongwon Choi), announced today that it will showcase its flagship wellness headband, Neuraon Assist, at CES 2027 in Las Vegas. Designed for modern individuals who struggle to unwind during hectic days or find themselves physically exhausted yet wide awake at bedtime, the device offers an effortless approach to daily stress relief and sleep preparation.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119851148/en/

815MNB’s Neuraon Assist wellness headband (Image: 815MNB)

William Marcel Sauve, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) at 815MNB, said, "Conventional wearable devices and stress scores can show people how their day has affected them, yet they still leave users to figure out what to do next." He added, "Neuraon Assist was born out of that familiar frustration. Instead of adding another layer of data to analyze, it eases that burden by automatically adjusting stimulation while the wearer simply takes a break."

At the core of Neuraon Assist is a proprietary closed-loop biofeedback system. The lightweight headband continuously tracks the user’s heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV), compares the readings against their personal baseline patterns, and delivers gentle, personalized noninvasive vagus nerve stimulation (VNS). It then measures the wearer’s real-time physiological response to dynamically guide the next adjustment. This automated process allows users to rest deeply without having to interpret complicated charts, interact with smartphone apps, or manually change settings throughout a session.

Alongside its growing consumer wellness business, 815MNB is actively expanding its research and development pipeline into specialized therapeutic applications. Current research initiatives explore potential interventions for developmental disabilities, cognitive health in older adults, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and behavioral or substance addictions involving gambling, drugs, or alcohol. The company expects to begin launching commercial products stemming from this clinical research in 2028.

About 815MNB

815MNB is a South Korean wearable technology innovator dedicated to developing closed-loop, bio-signal-based wellness and therapeutic solutions. By bridging real-time physiological monitoring with noninvasive neuromodulation, 815MNB aims to improve daily relaxation, restorative sleep, and long-term cognitive well-being. For more information, please visit www.815mnb.com.

815MNB
Yongwon Choi

data.title: Sunlands Technology Group Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE: STG) (“Sunlands” or the “Company”), a leader in China’s adult online education market and China’s adult personal interest learning market, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Snapshots

  • Net revenues were RMB331.6 million (US$49.5 million), compared to RMB523.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross billings (non-GAAP) were RMB239.0 million (US$35.6 million), compared to RMB349.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross profit was RMB273.4 million (US$40.8 million), compared to RMB462.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net income was RMB35.2 million (US$5.2 million), compared to RMB125.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net income margin1 was 10.6%, compared to 24.0% in the third quarter of 2025.
  • New student enrollments2 were 84,879, compared to 137,493 in the third quarter of 2025.
  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s deferred revenue balance was RMB382.5 million (US$57.1 million), compared to RMB585.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

_____________________________

1 Net income margin is defined as net income as a percentage of net revenues.
2 New student enrollments for a given period refer to the total number of orders placed by students that newly enroll in at least one course during that period, including those students that enroll and then terminate their enrollment with us, excluding orders of our low-price courses, such as “mini courses” and “RMB1 courses”, which we offer in the form of recorded videos or short live streaming, to strengthen our competitiveness and improve customer experience.

Mr. Tongbo Liu, Chief Executive Officer of Sunlands, commented, “During the third quarter of 2026, we remained focused on our core business, refining our course offerings and teaching services to better address evolving learner needs. As demand for lifelong learning among middle-aged and senior learners continues to diversify, we are placing greater emphasis on course quality, personalized learning experiences, and long-term learner engagement. Looking ahead, we will continue to build on our experience in adult education, further integrate technology into teaching and services, and strengthen our core business to support sustainable development.”

Mr. Hangyu Li, Finance Director of Sunlands, added, “In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues were RMB331.6 million and net income was RMB35.2 million, representing net income margin of 10.6%. Against a lower revenue base, we reduced operating expenses by 25.3% year-over-year and remained profitable for the 22nd consecutive quarter. We remain focused on aligning costs and resource allocation with our operating needs, preserving liquidity, and allocating capital prudently to support our core business and long-term development.”

Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026

Net Revenues

In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues decreased by 36.6% to RMB331.6 million (US$49.5 million) from RMB523.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the year-over-year decline in gross billings.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues decreased by 3.6% to RMB58.1 million (US$8.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB60.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined service fees paid to educational institutions.

Gross Profit

Gross profit decreased by 40.9% to RMB273.4 million (US$40.8 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB462.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Operating Expenses

In the third quarter of 2026, operating expenses were RMB242.2 million (US$36.1 million), representing a 25.3% decrease from RMB324.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 26.4% to RMB206.0 million (US$30.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB279.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the decreases of compensation for sales personnel and the spending on branding and marketing activities focused on interest courses offerings.

General and administrative expenses decreased by 18.7% to RMB29.2 million (US$4.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB36.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Product development expenses decreased by 18.9% to RMB7.0 million (US$1.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB8.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined compensation expenses related to the Company’s product development personnel.

Net Income

Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB35.2 million (US$5.2 million), as compared to RMB125.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share

Basic and diluted net income per share was RMB5.53 (US$0.83) in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to RMB18.64 in the third quarter of 2025.

Cash, Cash Equivalents, Restricted Cash and Short-term Investments

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had RMB502.0 million (US$74.9 million) of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash and RMB281.4 million (US$42.0 million) of short-term investments, as compared to RMB576.8 million of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash and RMB235.9 million of short-term investments as of December 31, 2025.

Deferred Revenue

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a deferred revenue balance of RMB382.5 million (US$57.1 million), as compared to RMB585.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

Share Repurchase

On May 29, 2026, the Company’s board of directors authorized a share repurchase program, under which the Company may repurchase up to US$50.0 million of Class A ordinary shares in the form of ADSs over the next 36 months. As of November 17, 2026, the Company had repurchased an aggregate of 716,479 ADSs for approximately US$2.4 million under the share repurchase program.

Financial Results for the First Nine Months of 2026

Net Revenues

In the first nine months of 2026, net revenues decreased by 23.9% to RMB1,178.6 million (US$175.8 million) from RMB1,549.7 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the year-over-year decline in gross billings.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues decreased by 13.6% to RMB174.9 million (US$26.1 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB202.3 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined cost of revenues from sales of goods such as learning materials and books and decreased service fees paid to educational institutions.

Gross Profit

Gross profit decreased by 25.5% to RMB1,003.7 million (US$149.7 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB1,347.4 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Operating Expenses

In the first nine months of 2026, operating expenses were RMB792.2 million (US$118.2 million), representing a 21.4% decrease from RMB1,008.1 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 23.4% to RMB676.2 million (US$100.9 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB882.7 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the decreases of compensation for sales personnel and the spending on branding and marketing activities focused on interest courses offerings.

General and administrative expenses decreased by 6.4% to RMB96.9 million (US$14.5 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB103.6 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Product development expenses decreased by 12.5% to RMB19.1 million (US$2.9 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB21.9 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Net Income

Net income for the first nine months of 2026 was RMB195.5 million (US$29.2 million), compared with RMB327.3 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share

Basic and diluted net income per share was RMB29.79 (US$4.44) in the first nine months of 2026, compared with RMB48.50 in the first nine months of 2025.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Sunlands currently expects net revenues to be between RMB220 million to RMB240 million, which would represent a decrease of between 49.0% to 53.2% year-over-year. The above outlook is based on the current market conditions and reflects the Company’s current and preliminary estimates of market and operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to substantial uncertainty.

Exchange Rate

The Company’s business is primarily conducted in China and all revenues are denominated in Renminbi (“RMB”). This announcement contains currency conversions of RMB amounts into U.S. dollars (“US$”) solely for the convenience of the reader. Unless otherwise noted, all translations from RMB to US$ are made at a rate of RMB6.7045 to US$1.00, the effective noon buying rate for September 30, 2026 as set forth in the H.10 statistical release of the Federal Reserve Board. No representation is made that the RMB amounts could have been, or could be, converted, realized or settled into US$ at that rate on September 30, 2026, or at any other rate.

About Sunlands

Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE: STG) (“Sunlands” or the “Company”), formerly known as Sunlands Online Education Group, is a leader in China’s adult online education market and China’s adult personal interest learning market. With a one to many live streaming platform, Sunlands offers various degree- or diploma-oriented post-secondary courses as well as professional certification preparation, professional skills and interest courses. Students can access the Company's services either through PC or mobile applications. The Company's online platform cultivates a personalized, interactive learning environment by featuring a virtual learning community and a vast library of educational content offerings that adapt to the learning habits of its students. Sunlands offers a unique approach to education research and development that organizes subject content into Learning Outcome Trees, the Company's proprietary knowledge management system. Sunlands has a deep understanding of the educational needs of its prospective students and offers solutions that help them achieve their goals.

About Non-GAAP Financial Measures

We use gross billings, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP operating cost and expenses, non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP net income per share, each a non-GAAP financial measure, in evaluating our operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes.

We define gross billings for a specific period as the total amount of cash received for the sale of course packages, net of the total amount of refunds paid in such period. Our management uses gross billings as a performance measurement because we generally bill our students for the entire course tuition at the time of sale of our course packages and recognize revenue proportionally over a period. EBITDA is defined as net income excluding depreciation and amortization, interest expense, interest income, and income tax expenses. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income excluding depreciation and amortization, interest expense, interest income, income tax expenses and impairment loss on long-lived assets. We believe that gross billings, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA provide valuable insight into the sales of our course packages and the performance of our business.

These non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, their most directly comparable financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of the historical non-GAAP financial measures to their respective most directly comparable GAAP measure has been provided in the tables included below. Investors are encouraged to review the reconciliation of the historical non-GAAP financial measures to their respective most directly comparable GAAP financial measures. As gross billings, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, operating cost and expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, general and administrative expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, sales and marketing expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, product development expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, income from operations excluding share-based compensation expenses, and basic and diluted net income per share excluding share-based compensation expenses have material limitations as an analytical metric and may not be calculated in the same manner by all companies, they may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures used by other companies. In light of the foregoing limitations, you should not consider gross billings, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA as a substitute for, or superior to, their respective most directly comparable financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. We encourage investors and others to review our financial information in its entirety and not rely on a single financial measure.

Sunlands may also make written or oral forward-looking statements in its reports filed with or furnished to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, in its annual report to shareholders, in press releases and other written materials and in oral statements made by its officers, directors or employees to third parties. Any statements that are not historical facts, including statements about Sunlands' beliefs and expectations, are forward-looking statements that involve factors, risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements. Such factors and risks include, but are not limited to the following: Sunlands’ goals and strategies; its expectations regarding demand for and market acceptance of its brand and services; its ability to retain and increase student enrollments; its ability to offer new courses and educational content; its ability to improve teaching quality and students’ learning results; its ability to improve sales and marketing efficiency and effectiveness; its ability to engage, train and retain new faculty members; its future business development, results of operations and financial condition; its ability to maintain and improve technology infrastructure necessary to operate its business; competition in the online education industry in China; relevant government policies and regulations relating to Sunlands’ corporate structure, business and industry; and general economic and business condition in China. Further information regarding these and other risks, uncertainties or factors is included in Sunlands' filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. data.title: Zoomlion Chairman Zhan Chunxin Meets Australian Customers to Strengthen Long-Term Partnerships
data.description:
Zoomlion Chairman Zhan Chunxin Meets Australian Customers to Strengthen Long-Term Partnerships

Zoomlion Chairman Zhan Chunxin Meets Australian Customers to Strengthen Long-Term Partnerships

PR Newswire

SYDNEY, Nov. 19, 2026

SYDNEY, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zoomlion Heavy Industry Science & Technology Co., Ltd. How does Zoomlion support customers in Australia?

Zoomlion has expanded its operations to five regional business centres in Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, and Adelaide since entering the Australian market in 2008. Originally set up as sales support locations, these sites have gradually taken on a broader role as regional business centres. The company now offers equipment across all its product categories in Australia. Through increased investment in the country in 2026, Zoomlion strengthened its service network and extended coverage beyond major regional hubs to make local support more accessible and improve its ability to respond to service requests.

These efforts form part of Zoomlion's broader global customer service initiative, which includes more than 30 local service hotlines supported by a global call centre. Australian customers can request technical assistance through their local hotline, and Zoomlion's service teams can coordinate repairs, spare parts, and on-site support.

Participating customers welcomed the opportunity to engage directly with Zoomlion's senior leadership. They said the visit reflected the importance Zoomlion placed on the Australian market. They praised the Company's product quality, technical support, and local services and expressed confidence in the prospects for further cooperation. Wang reaffirmed Zoomlion's commitment to its Australian partners by highlighting plans to expand local investment and strengthen the delivery of technology, equipment, and services tailored to customer requirements.

Moving forward, Zoomlion will continue investing in its Australian service network to make local support more accessible and build on longstanding customer relationships.

data.title: Winamp Group: Bridger Partners With Groover to Offer Copyright Royalty Collection to the Music Promotion Platform’s Artists
data.description:
Winamp Group: Bridger Partners With Groover to Offer Copyright Royalty Collection to the Music Promotion Platform’s Artists

Groover, a music promotion platform, reports more than 900,000 artists and labels · A further step in the execution of Bridger’s roadmap · A new acquisition channel for Bridger and Winamp for Artists

Regulatory News:

Winamp Group SA (Euronext Growth Paris and Brussels: ALWIN) announces a partnership between Bridger, its copyright management company, and Groover, the platform that connects independent artists with curators, media outlets, radio stations and labels.

The issue is a familiar one. Independent artists rely on a distributor to collect revenue from their recordings, yet the copyright royalties their songs generate, mechanical and performance royalties, often go unclaimed. The partnership brings together two complementary areas of expertise: Groover helps artists get their music in front of curators, media and radio, while Bridger collects the copyright royalties generated every time that music is streamed or broadcast.

A frictionless offer for Groover artists

Through a dedicated page, Groover artists can entrust Bridger with collecting their copyright royalties across more than 80 digital platforms, as well as from radio, television, live performances and public venues in more than 50 countries. Signing up is free and takes just a few minutes. Artists can claim up to 18 months of unpaid royalties and keep around 90% of the amounts collected.

A new acquisition channel for the Group

Groover artists are already investing in promoting their music, which makes them a close match for the established, career-focused projects the Group is prioritising. The partnership is part of the roadmap presented on 5 November, which continues to be rolled out: growing artist acquisition through partners that already work with artists every day.

Since 5 November, Bridger and Winamp have shared the same platform. An artist who joins Bridger for copyright collection can therefore move straight on to the other services offered by Winamp for Artists: distribution, licensing, website building, Fanzone and merchandising.

“For independent artists, getting heard and getting paid are part of the same fight. Groover helps them find their audience, and Bridger makes sure they receive the royalties they are owed. This partnership opens the door to a very large community of artists who are already investing in their careers, and each of them will then be able to discover everything Winamp for Artists has to offer.”
Alexandre Saboundjian, CEO, Winamp Group

NEXT EVENT

ABOUT WINAMP GROUP
Based in Brussels and listed on Euronext Growth Paris and Brussels (ALWIN), Winamp Group is building an ecosystem of services for independent artists and their fans. The Group brings together Winamp, Bridger, Jamendo and Hotmix, and offers music distribution, rights management, licensing, promotion and monetisation solutions.

An independent copyright management entity based in Luxembourg and a CISAC client Rights Management Entity, Bridger enables songwriters and composers to register their works and collect their royalties internationally, through a network of agreements with collective management organisations.

Founded in Paris in 2018, Groover is a music promotion platform that lets independent artists send their tracks to the curators, playlist editors, media outlets, radio stations and labels of their choice, with guaranteed feedback. It reports more than 900,000 artists and labels and over 3,500 curators and music professionals.

data.title: Japan Tobacco to Book $8.6 Billion Loss on Russia Business
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka

Japan Tobacco expects to book an $8.6 billion loss after losing control of its Russian business.

The Japanese tobacco maker said Thursday that it can no longer make business decisions concerning its operations in Russia in the same manner as before.

Earlier this month, Japan Tobacco said all seven of its Russian entities had been placed under temporary administration by a Russian company on the orders of President Vladimir Putin.

The move marked an escalation in Russian measures against Japanese businesses following Tokyo's support for Ukraine and its participation in Western sanctions against Moscow over its 2022 invasion.

Japan Tobacco on Thursday projected a net loss of Y724.00 billion, equivalent to $4.54 billion, for 2026, primarily due to a special loss of Y1.377 trillion related to the loss of control of its Russian business.

The company's Russian operations had about Y1.5 trillion in assets, including goodwill and roughly Y360 billion in cash and deposits, as well as about Y200 billion in liabilities at the end of September, the company said.

Japan Tobacco had expected Russia to account for about 10% of its revenue and 25% of adjusted operating profit in 2026.

The Japanese company was previously a state-owned monopoly, but the government held just under 38% of its shares at the end of 2025.

Japan Tobacco, whose brands include Winston and Camel, is one of Russia's largest tobacco companies, with a market share of nearly 40%.

data.title: Evotec and Bristol Myers Squibb Advance Strategic Protein Degradation Partnership with Second IND Acceptance
data.description:
Evotec and Bristol Myers Squibb Advance Strategic Protein Degradation Partnership with Second IND Acceptance

Evotec and Bristol Myers Squibb Advance Strategic Protein Degradation Partnership with Second IND Acceptance

PR Newswire

HAMBURG, Germany, Nov. 19, 2026
  • FDA clearance expands partnered molecular glue pipeline
  • Achievement underscores productivity of the collaboration in molecular glue discovery and potential to address patient populations with high unmet need

HAMBURG, Germany, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evotec SE (NASDAQ: EVO) (Frankfurt Prime Standard: EVT) today announced that its strategic protein degradation partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb has received a second Investigational New Drug (IND) acceptance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The first candidate produced under the partnership entered a Phase 1 clinical trial in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma in March 2026. The second accepted investigational drug candidate, a cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD), is expected to enter a Phase 1 clinical trial in 2027.

Initiated in 2018, the partnership combines Evotec's high-performance multi-omics screening, AI-supported data analytics, and drug design capabilities with Bristol Myers Squibb's industry-leading CELMoD agent library. This collaboration, expanded in 2022, continues to advance a pipeline of novel molecular glue degraders for high-value targets in oncology and beyond, translating scientific innovation into a growing therapeutic pipeline.

Dr. Joanna Holbrook, Chief Scientific Officer of Evotec, commented:

"The progression of a second molecular glue candidate to IND acceptance demonstrates the repeatability and productivity of our discovery platform. We are systematically translating complex biology into development candidates. This achievement reinforces the value of our longstanding collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb and further strengthens our confidence in the platform's potential to generate a growing pipeline of investigational drug candidates aimed at addressing substantial unmet medical needs."

About molecular glue degraders

Conventional small molecule therapeutics act through drug-induced interference with protein activity. This limitation to agonistic or antagonistic functions renders about 90% of proteins 'undruggable'. Also, conventional small molecules only work while they are actively binding to the receptor, which typically requires a treatment regimen consisting of one or even several carefully dosed medications every day.

Molecular glue degraders are compounds that induce interactions between an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a molecular target. The induced interaction results in ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of the recruited protein. By inducing neomorphic interactions between CRBN and substrate proteins, CELMoDs enable pharmacological modulation of proteins that may not be amenable to traditional inhibitor or agonist approaches, thereby expanding the potentially druggable proteome.

About Evotec's strategic collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb in molecular glues

In 2018, Evotec entered a long-term strategic drug discovery and development collaboration in the field of molecular glues with Celgene, now Bristol Myers Squibb. Bristol Myers Squibb is a leader in this field based on its unique library of CELMoD agents. The collaboration aims to discover and develop a leading pipeline of molecular glue degraders for a range of therapeutic indications leveraging all of Evotec's proprietary PanOmics and PanHunter platforms as well as AI/ML-based drug discovery and development capabilities.

Evotec applies high-end proteomics and transcriptomics at industrial scale to profile and select promising drug candidates based on comprehensive cell biological profiles. Evotec's leading PanOmics screening capabilities are delivering unmatched throughput. The selection of the most promising candidates for drug development is facilitated by Evotec's PanOmics data analysis platform PanHunter. By integrating and analyzing these data sets, PanHunter supports the identification and advancement of the most promising CELMoDs into lead optimization.

About Evotec SE

Evotec is a life science company pioneering the future of drug discovery and development. By integrating breakthrough science with AI-driven innovation and advanced technologies, Evotec accelerates the journey from concept to cure with greater speed, intelligence and precision. The company's expertise spans small molecules, biologics, cell therapies and associated modalities, supported by proprietary platforms including Molecular Patient Databases, PanOmics and induced pluripotent stem cell-based disease modeling. Through flexible partnering models tailored to customers' needs, Evotec works with all Top 20 pharmaceutical companies, more than 800 biotechnology companies, academic institutions and other healthcare stakeholders. Evotec's offerings range from standalone services to fully integrated research and development programs and long-term strategic partnerships, combining scientific excellence with operational agility. Through Just - Evotec Biologics, the company is redefining biologics development and manufacturing to improve accessibility and affordability. With a portfolio of more than 100 proprietary research and development assets, most of which are co-owned, Evotec focuses on key therapeutic areas including oncology, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurology and immunology. Evotec's global team of around 4,500 experts operates from sites in Europe and the United States, providing complementary technologies and services through a network of synergistic centers of excellence. data.title: Sanofi Gets U.S. Approval for Rare Disease Drug
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Sanofi received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for a new drug for a rare inherited disorder called Gaucher disease, the first treatment for neurological symptoms caused by the condition.

The French drugmaker said late Wednesday that its medicine, marketed under the Infilbray brand and also known as venglustat, was authorized in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kilograms--or 33 pounds--for type 3 Gaucher disease, one of the three major forms of the disease.

The FDA said type 3 Gaucher disease affects the brain and nervous system as harmful substances build up in the brain, causing difficulties with coordination, speech and thinking that can worsen over time.

Sanofi said Infilbray is a once-daily oral medicine designed to act across the blood-brain barrier, targeting the abnormal accumulation of fatty substances called glycosphingolipids.

A late-stage clinical trial showed the drug led to significant improvements in certain neurological manifestations of the disease like cognitive deficits and difficulty with coordination and balance, the company said.

Sanofi said Infilbray carries warnings and precautions for suicidal ideation and behavior, clouding of vision in younger patients, and adverse effects on fetal development during pregnancy.

data.title: Treasury Yields Fall in Asian Trade, Shrug off Fed Rate Hike Prospect
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields fall in Asian trade on Thursday, even as the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting showed readiness to raise interest rates further, potentially at a fast pace.

Minutes of the latest Fed rate-setting meeting, where the Fed left interest rates unchanged, indicated that some policymakers are leaning toward a larger-than-usual increase of half a percentage point in December. The committee's discussion of inflation revealed increasing concern of broadening price pressure amid strong growth in economic activity, Stuart Paul, U.S. economist at UBS, said in a note.

The minutes pushed higher market expectations of a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike on the Dec. 9 meeting. Money markets currently price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point hike in December and an 8% likelihood of a 50-basis-point tightening, according to LSEG. A 50-basis-point high was priced with a 2% probability on Wednesday.

"Strong data since the meeting is likely to have strengthened the case for further tightening and we see it as likely that members will indicate another rate increase in their projections in December," Elisabet Kopelman, U.S. economist and Fed watcher at SEB said. "We stick to our view of one more rate increase in December but risks are clearly skewed for another increase, possibly in March," she said.

The two-year Treasury yield slipped 0.4 basis points to 4.795%, while the 10-year Treasury yield declined also 0.4 basis point to 5.061%, according to Tradeweb.

The Treasury will conduct a $19 billion auction of 10-year Treasury inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, on Thursday.

Despite the backdrop of higher real yields, cheap valuations, and improving liquidity, J.P. Morgan analysts think the hawkish Fed backdrop and amount of supply in the 10-year sector means the auction "will need more of a concession to be digested smoothly."

data.title: South Korean Tourism Stocks Rally on Hopes for Expanded China Trade Pact
data.description:
By Kwanwoo Jun

South Korean tourism stocks rallied Thursday on hopes that an expanded free-trade agreement between Seoul and Beijing would boost Chinese visitor arrivals.

China and South Korea earlier this week reached a deal to broaden the scope of their 2015 FTA to include sectors such as tourism, entertainment and investment services, wrapping up years of negotiations, according to President Lee Jae Myung's office in Seoul.

The deal, announced Wednesday after a bilateral summit between Lee and his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, allows South Korean travel agencies to organize outbound travel from 23 regions in China, according to South Korea's trade ministry.

In Seoul trading Thursday, travel company Hanatour Service jumped as much as 28%, while budget airline Jeju Air climbed up to 25%. Hotel Shilla, which operates hotels and duty-free shops, rose as much as 13%.

"The expansion of channels to attract Chinese tourists to South Korea is expected to further boost passenger demand on China routes," Hanwha Investment & Securities analyst Park Su-young said after the deal was reached.

The aviation, entertainment and leisure industries stand to gain from the latest Korea-China pact, with aviation likely to be the biggest beneficiary, she wrote in a research note.

Hana Securities analyst Dohyun Ahn viewed Jeju Air as a key beneficiary of the expanded FTA, citing the company's greater exposure to the Chinese market than any other South Korean low-cost carrier.

Routes to mainland China account for 8% of the South Korean budget airline's revenue, and that share could increase further, Ahn said.

In a statement on Wednesday's expanded deal, President Lee's office said South Korea and China should continue immigration measures to facilitate travel between the two countries to help boost bilateral people-to-people exchanges.

The office expects the number of people traveling between the two countries to reach 10 million this year and hopes it will eventually return to the 13 million recorded in 2016.

Exchanges have been constrained since Beijing allegedly restricted Chinese group tours to South Korea following Seoul's decision in 2016 to deploy a U.S. missile-defense system despite Chinese protests. Beijing has denied imposing a ban.
